Counsel for Opposite Party(s) 
Anil Sharma vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 6 November, 2025
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned AGA for the State.
Supplementary affidavit filed today is taken on record.

2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in Crime No. 16/2025, under Sections 281, 125(a),
125(b), 105, 324(2) B.N.S., Police Station - Itaunja, District - Lucknow.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that in terms of the FIR it was alleged that the applicant, driving a container, caused an accident resulting in death.
The supplementary affidavit indicates even compensation has been received under Motor Vehicles Act.
Thus, the implication of the applicant under Section 105 BNS is prima facie not made out.
4. Learned AGA has opposed the bail application.

5. Considering compensation has been received and ingredients of Section 105 BNS coupled with the fact that the applicant is in custody since 30.01.2025 and has no criminal antecedent, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant- Anil Sharma be released on bail in aforesaid FIR/Case Crime Number subject to his furnishing a personal bond and two reliable sureties of Rs. 20,000/- (Twenty Thousand) each of the like amount with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(Pankaj Bhatia,J.) November 6, 2025 Mohit Singh/-
